 SCCH 15 3 MVC No.3353/2017  JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 75,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 24.10.2016 at about 7.00 p.m., when the Petitioner was travelling as a passenger in Trax Cruser vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-28-N-5749 from Bengaluru to Bijapur and when it reached near Bennehalli village, NH-13, at that time, one Car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B-1759 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the said Trax Cruser vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-28-N-5749 and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner along with other inmates had sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Chitradurga District Hospital for treatment and after first aid she was referred to NIMHANS and she was admitted an an inpatient in the said hospital.
Further, she had undergone surgery in the said hospital.

2 4.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was doing Tailoring and embroidery work and was earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month.

Due to the accidental injuries, she became paraplegia and due to uncontrolled urination the Petitioner had undergone surgery for fixation of Catheter for free urination and for her entire her she has to continue the same.
Due to the injuries sustained the Petitioner had suffered great mental shock, bodily pain and sufferings and she became permanently disabled.
The said accident has been occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Indigo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B-1759 by its driver.

The Respondent No.1 is the Owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B-1759 SCCH 15 5 MVC No.3353/2017 and the Respondent No.3 is the owner and the Respondent No.4 is the insurer of the Trax Cruser vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-28-N-5749.
Therefore, all Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 to 4 had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels.
But, the Respondent No.3 did not choose to file Objection Statement to the main petition.
The Respondent No.2 and 4 had filed their detailed Objection Statements.

6. The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B-1759 and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.

Further it contended that the driver of the offending SCCH 15 6 MVC No.3353/2017 vehicle i.e., Tata Car does not hold valid and effective DL and the said vehicle does not had valid Permit and Fitness Certificate to ply on the public place.
The owner of the said vehicle has allowed the driver to drive the same who did not hold valid and effective driving license and thereby there is clear violation of the policy terms and conditions.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
7. The Respondent No.4 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.
Further it admitted that it has issued policy in respect of the Trax Cruser vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-28-N-5749.

Further it contended that there is no negligence of the Trax Cruser vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-28-N- 5749 and it denied other allegations made in the petition and has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

On the other hand, the Respondents did not choose to lead oral or documentary evidence.
At the initial, after trail and after hearing arguments by both side, this Tribunal has passed Judgment and Award on 06.03.2019 by partly allowing the claim petition field by the Petitioner.

Being aggrieved by the said Judgment and Award dated 13.08.2018, The Petitioner preferred an Appeal in MFA No. 6883 of 2019(MV-I) before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru and also filed I.A No.1 and the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to passed the order dated 22.02.2024 by allowing I.A No.1 and set aside the Judgement and award passed by this tribunal and remanded the case to the tribunal for a fresh consideration in accordance with law and passed order by giving liberty to both the parties to adduce oral or documentary evidence if so desired and also directed to refer the appellant to the Medical Board Nimhans, Bengaluru for assessing the disability and after receiving the report from the Medical Board and considering the evidence on record dispose the case afresh in accordance with law.

sentences.text: Issue No.1:-

It is the case of the Petitioner that, she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 24.10.2016 at about 7.00 p.m by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Indigo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B-1759 by its driver.
15. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Indigo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B-1759 by its driver.
16. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, she got examined herself as PW.2 through Court Commissioner and got marked 10 documents at Ex.C.1 to Ex.C.10.

She also examined the Junior Medical record Incharge Officer of Nimhans by name Rajanna S.K as PW.1 and got marked 3 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P3.
SCCH 15 11 MVC No.3353/2017 17.
After remand, the Petitioner has filed her further chief affidavit in lieu of further chief examination and got marked one document at Ex.P4 and closed her side evidence.

18. Upon going through the documents exhibited i.e., Ex.C.1 and Ex.C2 are the FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by one Balachandra S/o Shanthappa Kadakol, the Jagalur Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B- 1759 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.C.3 and 5 are the Spot Sketch and Mahazar which shows that the Jagalur police had drawn mahazar and Sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.C4 is the Statement of the Petitioner and Ex.C6 and 7 are the Indemnity bonds.

Ex.C8 is the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Jagalur Traffic Police Station has submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg No. KA-16-B-1759 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
Ex.C9 is the Rent Agreement SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3353/2017 and Renewal Agreement.
Ex.C10 is the Aadhar card of the Petitioner.
Ex.P1 to 3 are the authorization letter, MLC and Case Sheet of the Petitioner.
PW.2 is subjected for cross examination by the Learned counsel for Respondent No.2.
But, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.2.
It is pertinent to note here that, the Police documents have not been challenged by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further, the Respondent No.1 being the RC owner of the offending Car did not appear before the Court despite of service of the notice to him.

Though Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle had appeared before the court and contested the matter by filing the Objection Statement to the main Petition, it did not choose to examine any of the witness to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.

sentences.text: The Case sheet which is produced by the PW.1 shows that she had sustained grievous injuries.

The Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation, the Investigation SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3353/2017 Officer has submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the car bearing Reg No.
KA-16-B-1759.
20.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioner and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the alleged accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B-1759 and in the said accident, she sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "In the Affirmative."

21. Issue No.2: As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Indigo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B-1759 by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
22. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown her age as 56 years.

Further, in the Aadhar card i.e.,
Ex.C-10, the date of birth of the Petitioner was shown as 01.01.1963.
The accident has taken place on 24.10.2016.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the Petitioner was 53 years, 9 months and SCCH 15 14 MVC No.3353/2017 24 days.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident was 54 years and the same to be taken for consideration.
23. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, she was doing Tailoring and Embroidery work and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
But, she has not produced any document in this regard.

Therefore,
in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.9,500/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
24. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
25.
In the Petition, the Petitioner has stated that she had sustained grievous injuries.

The Case sheet i.e., Ex.P-3 issued by the Medical Officer of the NIMHANS Hospital, SCCH 15 15 MVC No.3353/2017 Bengaluru shows that at the time of admission in the said hospital they noticed weakness of all four limbs of the Petitioner and she could not lift her legs and only partially lift both upper limbs.

sentences.text: Further it shows that immediately after the injury, she was taken to Chitradurga Government Hospital, where she was catheterised because she was not able to pass urine, after which she was referred to NIMHANS.

26. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.75,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
II.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :

SCCH 15 16 MVC No.3353/2017 III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
28. The Petitioner deposed in her evidence that she has taken treatment as an inpatient at Nimhans Hospital.
Ex.P.3 is the Case sheet of Nimhans Hospital.
It shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Nimhans Hospital from 27.10.2016 to 10.11.2016 and 11.11.2016 to 15.11.2016.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 20 days.
29. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as four months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.38,000/- under this head (@ Rs.9,500/- per month ).
 IV.

COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
 SCCH 15 17 MVC No.3353/2017 30.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also she might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for her conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs. 12,000/- (@ Rs.100/- per day) towards attendants charges, Rs.12,000/-
towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.12,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.36,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
31. The Petitioner has deposed that she has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
Further she admitted in her cross examination that the entire medical bills were reimbursed.
Hence, she is not entitled any compensation under this head.

SCCH 15 18 MVC No.3353/2017 VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS /
COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
32.
The Petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by her in the accident, she has suffered permanent disablement and she is not able to do her work as she used to do earlier.
Even in her evidence, P.W.2 has deposed to that effect.

sentences.text: After remand of the case, the Petitioner was referred to Medical Board, NIMHANS, Benglauru for the assessment of disability.
Accordingly, the Medical Board, NIMHANS, Bengaluru has assessed the disability of the Petitioner at 81% in relation to all four limbs by neurogenic bladder(whole body), permanent in nature.
The Petitioner got marked the said report at Ex.P4.
She has denied the suggestion put-forth to her in the cross examination.
In the Petition as well as in the evidence of the Petitioner she has deposed that she was doing tailoring and embroidery work.
The Medical Board has SCCH 15 19 MVC No.3353/2017 assessed the physical disability of the Petitioner and it has not assessed the functional disability.
For the work of tailoring, all four limbs are essential, particularly lower limb is important.

Hence, by considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the evidence of the PW.2 and the disability assessed by the Medical Board and by considering the avocation of the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the functional disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 100% would be just and proper.
34. In the case on hand, the notional income of the Petitioner to be taken at Rs.9,500/- p.m in the absence of proof of income.
The age of the Petitioner as on the date of the accident was 54 years.
Hence, If 10% of the income of the Petitioner i.e., Rs.950/- is taken as future prospects, then the total income comes to Rs.10,450/-.
The multiplier applicable is 11.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future earning due to disability is Rs.13,79,400/-.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,79,400/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
35.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 75,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 75,000/-
3. Loss of income during the Rs. 38,000/-
laid up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 36,000/- diet, and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses Rs. -
6. Loss of Future Income Rs. 13,79,400/-
Total Rs
36 . Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs. 16,03,400/- with costs and simple interest.

Hence, now the Petitioner is entitled to receive the compensation after deduction of the said Rs.1,40,000/- from the total compensation amount of Rs.16,03,400/- i.e., Rs.14,63,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a, from the date of this Petitioner till the date of realization.

37. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Indigo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B-1759.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the R.C. Owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the Indigo Car bearing Reg.No.KA-16-B-1759.

It is pertinent to note here that this tribunal comes to the conclusion that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Trax Cruser bearing Reg.
NO.KA- 28-N-5749.
Hence, the Respondent No.3 and 4 are not liable to pay any compensation to the Petitioner.
Therefore, the SCCH 15 22 MVC No.3353/2017 Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
38. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.

The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs. 14,63,400/-
(Rs.16,03,400/- - Rs.1,40,000/-) along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from SCCH 15 23 MVC No.3353/2017 the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of five years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

34. In the case on hand, the notional income of the Petitioner to be taken at Rs.9,500/- p.m in the absence of proof of income.
Hence, If 10% of the income of the Petitioner i.e., Rs.950/- is taken as future prospects, then the total income comes to Rs.10,450/-.
The multiplier applicable is 11.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future earning due to disability is Rs.13,79,400/-.
(Rs.10,450 X 12 = 1,25,400/-, Rs.1,25,400 SCCH 15 20 MVC No.3353/2017 X 11 X 100/100=13,79,400/-)
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,79,400/- under this head.

36 . Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs. 16,03,400/- with costs and simple interest.

38. Issue No.3:
In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs. 14,63,400/-
(Rs.16,03,400/- - Rs.1,40,000/-) along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from SCCH 15 23 MVC No.3353/2017 the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 75% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of five years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
